issues.title: Excess shard-aware connection is dropped without decrementing total_connections
issues.verdictReason: In handle_ready_connection's `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` branch, the just-opened `connection` is dropped (only `start_opening_connection(None)` is called) without any call to `dec_total_connections`/`decrement_total_connections`, even though `inc_total_connections` fired when the connection was opened (start_opening_connection's count_in_metrics); this branch is byte-for-byte unchanged from main, so the leak predates this PR.
issues.scopeReason: The branch at connection_pool.rs:994-1006 is untouched by this diff; the PR's metrics-balancing commit fixed three other clearing sites (reshard, excess-limit-clear, full-pool-clear) but left this pre-existing one alone.

issues.title: Pool worker shutdown drops conns/excess_connections without decrementing total_connections
issues.verdictReason: When the use_keyspace request channel closes, run() returns at line 697 and `self` (with all of `self.conns` and `self.excess_connections`) is dropped without any dec_total_connections calls; the counter is purely manual (no Drop-based accounting on Connection), so this leaks the gauge. This return path is unchanged from main.
issues.scopeReason: This shutdown branch was not touched by the diff and the same gap existed before the metrics-balancing commit was written.

issues.title: Per-connection USE has no timeout, so a hang suppresses the promised keyspace-failure…
issues.verdictReason: start_setting_keyspace_for_connection awaits connection.use_keyspace(&keyspace_name) with no timeout wrapper; query_raw_unpaged/query_raw_with_consistency call send_request directly and never consult an execution profile or statement request_timeout, and RequestAttemptError has no timeout variant, so UseKeyspaceError::RequestTimeout (only reachable via the test's synthetic construction) is effectively unreachable from real traffic. A USE that hangs never completes, leaving is_filling() true indefinitely: the new keyspace-setup-error-triggers-refill fix added by this PR never fires, and update_shared_conns/Broken publication is suppressed for an empty pool.
issues.scopeReason: The missing timeout on the await predates the PR, but the PR's entire point is to guarantee that keyspace setup failures are detected and drive a refill; a hang defeats that guarantee for the exact feature this PR implements, so fixing it belongs here.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The per-connection USE still has no timeout. A USE that hangs never yields a keyspace setup error, so the promised refill never happens. / Sharder and port learning now has to wait for the per-connection USE, which still has no timeout. A hung USE delays resharding without limit, and while it is pending `is_filling()` stays true, which suppresses the Broken publication in the new keyspace arm.

issues.title: Keyspace regression test's QUERY rule never checks the request was actually USE
issues.verdictReason: make_rules's QUERY RequestRule matches any Condition::RequestOpcode(RequestOpcode::Query) frame and the reaction never inspects frame body/content to confirm it is the expected `USE <keyspace>` statement; in this specific test no other QUERY is sent so it happens to work, but the assertion is weaker than the test name implies and would silently pass even if a different query were sent.
issues.scopeReason: This fixture is new in this PR's regression test.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The keyspace regression fixture matches every QUERY opcode and never verifies that the connection sent the expected USE statement.
